---
title: "GWAS with low-pass data: three ways to handle structure"
output: html_document
---

```{r knitr-options, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 4)
```

Run the chunks in order. Set your paths and trait in the next chunk, run it, then run everything below it.

```{r settings}
WORKDIR     <- "."
ANGSD       <- "~/angsd/angsd"
BEAGLE      <- "WL2_2025_Stor_combined.beagle.gz"
FAI         <- "YO_2_1.fa.fai"
PCANGSD_COV <- "pcangsd_result/WL2_2025.cov"      # plant x plant covariance from PCAngsd
PHENO       <- "gwas/height.txt"                  # one value per plant, beagle order, -999 = missing
TRAIT       <- "height"
OUTDIR      <- "gwas"
N_PC        <- 10
THREADS     <- 7
CHROMS      <- NULL                               # NULL = all chromosomes in the results
RUN_ANGSD   <- FALSE                              # TRUE to run ANGSD, FALSE to only print the commands

source("gwas_helpers.R")
setwd(WORKDIR)
dir.create(OUTDIR, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
```

# Three runs

We test one trait at every SNP with the ANGSD latent genotype model. The three runs differ only in how they treat population structure.

1. No correction.
2. The top PCs as covariates.
3. The PCs as covariates, and the trait replaced by its residual from a mixed model with the PCAngsd relatedness matrix (rrBLUP).

Run 2 stays inflated on our data (lambda about 2), which is why run 3 is there. A stronger correction can also remove real signal, so we look at the QQ and Manhattan plots for all three.

# Inputs

The phenotype and the covariance matrix must list plants in the same order as the beagle file. The check below only compares counts, so also compare IDs yourself.

```{r inputs}
y <- as.numeric(readLines(PHENO))
y[y == -999] <- NA

C   <- unname(as.matrix(read.table(PCANGSD_COV)))
eig <- eigen(C, symmetric = TRUE)

n_beagle <- (length(strsplit(readLines(gzfile(BEAGLE), n = 1), "\t")[[1]]) - 3) / 3
stopifnot(length(y) == nrow(C), length(y) == n_beagle)
c(plants = length(y), with_phenotype = sum(!is.na(y)))
```

We rank-transform the trait to a normal distribution so a few extreme plants cannot drive a hit. PCs are scaled to mean 0 and sd 1.

```{r prepare}
ok <- !is.na(y)
y_int     <- rep(NA_real_, length(y))
y_int[ok] <- qnorm((rank(y[ok]) - 0.5) / sum(ok))

pcs <- scale(eig$vectors[, 1:N_PC])

write_pheno <- function(x, file) writeLines(ifelse(is.na(x), "-999", sprintf("%.6f", x)), file)
write_pheno(y_int, file.path(OUTDIR, paste0(TRAIT, "_int.txt")))
write.table(round(pcs, 6), file.path(OUTDIR, paste0("pcs", N_PC, ".txt")), row.names = FALSE, col.names = FALSE)

hist(y, breaks = 30, main = TRAIT, xlab = TRAIT)
```

# rrBLUP residual

The model is y = Xb + u + e. X is an intercept plus the PCs, u is a random effect with covariance Vu * K, where K is the PCAngsd matrix, and e is noise with variance Ve. We keep e as the new phenotype. A small value on the diagonal of K keeps it invertible.

```{r rrblup}
X <- cbind(1, pcs)[ok, ]
K <- C[ok, ok] + diag(1e-6, sum(ok))

fit <- rrBLUP::mixed.solve(y_int[ok], X = X, K = K)
res <- y_int[ok] - as.numeric(X %*% as.numeric(fit$beta)) - as.numeric(fit$u)
stopifnot(all(is.finite(res)))

y_resid     <- rep(NA_real_, length(y))
y_resid[ok] <- as.numeric(scale(res))
write_pheno(y_resid, file.path(OUTDIR, paste0(TRAIT, "_rrblup_resid.txt")))

c(Vu = fit$Vu, Ve = fit$Ve, share_relatedness = fit$Vu / (fit$Vu + fit$Ve))
```

`share_relatedness` is the part of the trait variance that follows relatedness after the PCs. Run 3 cannot map that part. The PC covariates stay in run 3 so the main ancestry axes are removed from the genotype side too.

# ANGSD

`-doAsso 4` is the latent genotype model. `-minHigh` and `-minCount` drop sites with too few informative plants or too few minor alleles. With `RUN_ANGSD <- FALSE` this only prints the three commands.

```{r angsd}
pheno_int <- file.path(OUTDIR, paste0(TRAIT, "_int.txt"))
pheno_res <- file.path(OUTDIR, paste0(TRAIT, "_rrblup_resid.txt"))
pc_file   <- file.path(OUTDIR, paste0("pcs", N_PC, ".txt"))

out <- c(`No correction` = file.path(OUTDIR, paste0(TRAIT, "_run1_nocov")),
         `PCs`          = file.path(OUTDIR, paste0(TRAIT, "_run2_pcs")),
         `rrBLUP`       = file.path(OUTDIR, paste0(TRAIT, "_run3_rrblup")))

asso <- function(pheno, out, cov = "") {
  paste(ANGSD, "-doMaf 4 -beagle", BEAGLE, "-fai", FAI, "-yQuant", pheno, cov,
        "-doAsso 4 -minHigh 10 -minCount 10 -P", THREADS, "-out", out)
}

cat(asso(pheno_int, out[1]),
    asso(pheno_int, out[2], paste("-cov", pc_file)),
    asso(pheno_res, out[3], paste("-cov", pc_file)),
    sep = "\n\n")

files <- paste0(out, ".lrt0.gz")
names(files) <- names(out)
```

# Results

```{r read}
stopifnot("Result files missing. Set RUN_ANGSD <- TRUE, run the settings chunk, then the ANGSD chunk." = all(file.exists(files)))
runs   <- map(files, read_lrt)
chroms <- if (is.null(CHROMS)) unique(runs[[1]]$chr) else CHROMS
lay    <- chr_layout(FAI, chroms)

tibble(run = names(runs), sites = map_int(runs, nrow), lambda = round(map_dbl(runs, lambda_gc), 2),
       threshold = round(bonferroni(sites), 2), sites_above = map_int(runs, ~ sum(.x$logp >= bonferroni(nrow(.x)))))
```

Lambda is the median test statistic divided by its value under no association. 1 means calibrated. `sites_above` counts sites past the Bonferroni line.

```{r qq, fig.width = 5, fig.height = 5}
iwalk(runs, function(d, nm) {
  p <- plot_qq(runs[nm]) +
    ggtitle(sprintf("%s: lambda = %.2f", nm, lambda_gc(d))) +
    theme(legend.position = "none")
  ggsave(file.path(OUTDIR, paste0(TRAIT, "_qq_", gsub(" ", "_", nm), ".png")), p, width = 5, height = 5, dpi = 300)
  print(p)
})
```

A calibrated run follows the diagonal and lifts off only at the far right. A run that lifts off early is inflated everywhere.

```{r manhattan, fig.width = 10, fig.height = 4}
iwalk(runs, function(d, nm) {
  p <- plot_manhattan(d, lay, title = nm)
  ggsave(file.path(OUTDIR, paste0(TRAIT, "_manhattan_", gsub(" ", "_", nm), ".png")), p, width = 10, height = 4, dpi = 300)
  print(p)
})
```
The red line is Bonferroni at 5%. A peak that holds in all three runs does not depend on how structure was handled. A peak that is only in run 1 is ancestry. A peak that is in run 2 and gone in run 3 could be fine-scale structure, or real signal absorbed by the mixed model. Check how much of the trait the PCs and relatedness explain before deciding which.
